audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with the loud, broadband rushing sound of a high-pressure water spray hitting a surface. A pop-style BGM with female vocals singing in English plays. A female speaker exclaims in a high-pitched, slightly distressed tone about the water. (2) The BGM transitions to a lighter, upbeat acoustic guitar melody. The sound of water pouring into a plastic container creates a resonant splashing sound. The female voice exclaims with high arousal, while a male voice responds in a calm, informative tone. (3) A professional male voice dominates, explaining water pipe biofilms. Rhythmic, percussive thuds—simulating the 'water hammer' effect—occur every 0.5 seconds against a low-volume musical bed. The acoustic guitar rhythm remains steady in the background. (4) The male narrator continues explaining technical aspects like citric acid cleaning and pressure testing. The sound environment is clean with moderate reverb, suggesting a tiled bathroom space. Brief sounds of water rushing through pipes and splashing in a sink punctuate the speech. (5) The video concludes with a final exclamation of disgust from the female voice as the sound of water sloshing in a bucket is heard. The acoustic BGM maintains its tempo until it fades out into silence as the narration ends.
